ck-registry-key/v1.served_as: GET /v1/registry/keys: {schema: 'ck-registry-keys/v1', registry, keys: [{statement, signature}]} in chain order from the first introduced key
ck-registry-key/v1.rule: each statement is signed by the newest key the client already holds for that registry, starting from the key pinned with the allowlist entry; a held key id or public key with other bytes is key_conflict; bytes already accepted are a duplicate

cases.name: successor_signed_by_current
cases.note: key 2 introduced by pinned key 1

cases.name: next_link
cases.note: key 3 introduced by key 2, the newest key held

cases.name: same_statement_again
cases.note: the chain is served whole on every fetch; links already held are no-ops

cases.name: skips_the_chain
cases.note: key 3 signed by key 1 while key 2 is the newest key held: only the chain counts

cases.name: self_signed
cases.note: a key cannot introduce itself

cases.name: bit_flip
cases.note: first signature byte XOR 0x01

cases.name: status_domain_tag
cases.note: signed under ck-status/v1 instead of ck-registry-key/v1

cases.name: other_registry
cases.note: a statement for another allowlisted registry

cases.name: key_id_reused
cases.note: a held key id with another key

cases.name: public_key_reused
cases.note: a held public key under a new id

ck-key-rotation/v1.served_as: {statement, old_signature, new_signature}; both signatures over the same signing input
order: key_unknown / key_revoked / key_not_valid (old key must be current)

cases.name: cross_signed
cases.note: old key authorizes, new key proves possession

cases.name: new_signature_by_old_key
cases.note: no proof that the submitter holds the new key

cases.name: record_domain_tag
cases.note: both signatures made under ck-record/v1

cases.name: old_key_not_in_scope
cases.note: key 2 signs correctly but is not in @example's set

cases.name: old_key_revoked
cases.note: a revoked key cannot hand over its scope

cases.name: old_key_retired
cases.note: only a current key can rotate

cases.name: new_key_was_in_a_scope
cases.note: a key ever in any scope's set is never added again

cases.name: other_scope
cases.note: submitted for @example but names @acme

cases.name: carries_valid_from
cases.note: the registry assigns valid_from; the statement may not

ck-key-cert/v1.served_as: {statement, signature} beside each @cortexkit key in GET /v1/scopes/cortexkit; verified against the compiled-in root public key

cases.name: open_ended_cert
cases.note: valid_until null: valid until a later cert or a revocation

cases.name: self_certified
cases.note: signed by the certified key itself

cases.name: signed_by_registry_key
cases.note: the registry can never make a key trusted

cases.name: record_domain_tag
cases.note: root signature under ck-record/v1

cases.name: other_scope
cases.note: the root certifies @cortexkit keys only

cases.name: empty_window
cases.note: valid_until must be later than valid_from

ck-status-request/v1.served_as: POST /v1/packages/{scope}/{name}/{version}/withdraw or /unwithdraw with body {statement, public_key, signature}
order: record_mismatch (action, name, version against the path)
key_unknown / key_revoked / key_not_valid (a current key of the scope)
status_sequence_conflict (after_sequence must equal the current sequence)
action_not_allowed (withdraw only from available, unwithdraw only from withdrawn)
